newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Britain doesn't plan to raise BSE formally at Farm Council.
newsitem.headline: Britain doesn't plan to raise BSE formally at Farm Council.

text.p: Britain will not formally raise the question of exempting herds certified to be free of mad cow disease from a worldwide ban on British beef exports at next week's EU Farm Council, British diplomats said on Friday.
But they added it would be discussed privately.
"BSE (Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy) is not on the official agenda," one diplomat said.

However British Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg and Scottish Secretary Michael Forsyth are likely to sound out EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler's views on the scheme when they see him privately on Monday.
"It's hard to imagine them not discussing BSE and the way forward," the diplomat said.
Technical discussions between British and Commission officials began two weeks ago on the definition of BSE-free herds and how the scheme would operate.
But progress is unlikely until after EU scientists have given their advice in mid-November on new British scientific studies casting doubt over a planned selective cull of cattle most at risk to BSE.
The cull was one of the conditions in a deal agreed by EU leaders in Florence in June for a gradual lifting of the seven months old British ban.
Exemption of certified herds would be a first step.
Transmittable spongiform encephalopathies will also be on the agenda of the next EU Health Council on November 12.
